text:
jenna (support): fyi customer (ACME) in their private VPC reports NXDOMAIN for api.redwood-prod.internal from their app containers. they also see TLS handshake errors to 10.2.12.5. VPC is vpc-0a1b2c3d. any quick thoughts?

mo (eng-sre): can you paste the dig + curl outputs?

jenna (support): sending their repro. note: they try both app container and host resolver.
```
# from app container (alpine)
$ dig api.redwood-prod.internal +short

# from amazon resolver in host namespace
$ dig @10.0.0.2 api.redwood-prod.internal +short
10.2.12.5

# curl from app (fails)
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-prod.internal/ --resolve api.redwood-prod.internal:443:10.2.12.5
* Connected to 10.2.12.5 (10.2.12.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: certificate mismatch / handshake fails
```

kevin (netops): two quick possibilities: 1) their app is using a local DNS cache that isn't forwarding to VPC resolver, or 2) Route53 private hosted zone not visible from their VPC (cross-account association / resolver rules). which account owns the private zone?

jenna (support): zone redwood-prod.internal is in our prod account (redwood-prod). customer is in their own aws account. they said they created a resolver rule to forward redwood-prod.internal to our inbound resolver endpoint (10.10.5.4), but still NXDOMAIN from app.

maria (eng): if they forward to our inbound endpoint, we need: (a) their outbound resolver rule associated with their VPC, (b) our inbound endpoint SG must allow UDP/TCP 53 from their VPC CIDR, and (c) NACLs/firewalls must allow that traffic. also containers sometimes have dnsStub disabled and use 127.0.0.11 (docker) which needs host resolv.conf to be correct.

mo (eng-sre): can they reach 10.10.5.4: try nc/tcping and also do a tcpdump on our inbound endpoint to see queries.

jenna (support): they ran connectivity checks, pasted below:
```
# from their app host
$ nc -vz 10.10.5.4 53
Connection to 10.10.5.4 53 port [tcp/domain] succeeded!

# but they also showed iptables egress rules that DROP UDP 53 from containers:
$ iptables -L OUTPUT -n | grep 53
DROP       udp -- 0.0.0.0/0            10.10.5.4           udp dpt:domain
```

kevin (netops): aha — egress is blocked for UDP 53 from containers. TCP 53 might succeed but DNS primarily uses UDP. ask them to allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to our resolver IPs or associate the private hosted zone with their VPC.

jenna (support): relayed that. they temporarily relaxed egress rule to allow 10.10.5.4/32 on UDP 53. reran dig from app: 
```
$ dig api.redwood-prod.internal +short
10.2.12.5
```
and curl --resolve now completes TLS handshake (certs match). they confirm app is working.

maria (eng): long-term options: 1) we can offer to associate the private hosted zone with their VPC (cross-account association) if policy allows, 2) they can keep resolver rule -> inbound endpoint, but must permanently allow outbound DNS to our inbound endpoints, 3) they can run a forwarder in their account that resolves to us and lives in the same VPC as containers. document which route they want.

kevin (netops): also double-check Route53: private hosted zone has to be associated with the VPC or resolved via resolver endpoint; cross-account associations must be explicitly added. i can check our console if you want — what's the hosted zone id?

jenna (support): hosted zone id Z1ABCDEF. customer prefers inbound endpoint path. they will update egress rules and add persistent allowlist.

deploy-bot: ticket TKT-4591 created for follow-up (associate endpoints + docs update).

mo (eng-sre): thanks everyone. two follow-ups for the runbook: add a quick checklist for customers using resolver rules -> 1) ensure resolver rule associated with VPC, 2) confirm outbound firewall allows UDP/TCP 53 to inbound endpoint IPs, 3) verify inbound endpoint SGs allow their VPC CIDR, 4) verify container DNS stub settings.

jenna (support): customer confirmed stable after egress change. closing unless anyone wants to keep open. :thumbsup:

kevin (netops): :thumbsup: closing from netops side.
